name: Cycads — sagos and relatives
status: 5 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: Living fossils: palm-like crowns, cones not flowers, beetle-pollinated, seeds by birds, rodents and sea. Centuries-old; a cycad grove is an old place. Seeds toxic unless leached, which camp folk know. Wood's cycad is a one-clone mythic plant.

shrub.name: Sago cycad

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal: the orange seed stays at the surface while a taproot and contractile roots pull the stem base down. First fronds are short and soft with few pairs of leaflets; a stemless rosette adds one flush of glossy, stiff, dark-green fronds a year over a bulb-like caudex that emerges as a stubby, shaggy trunk after 5-10 years.
growth.source: Monaco Nature Encyclopedia (one flush of leaves a year, to 6-7 m, plants several hundred years old; insect pollination May-July; seeds red-orange 3-5 cm, ripe Sep-Oct; germination 50-100 d); Kono & Tobe 2007 Am. J. Bot. (beetle Carpophilus plus wind); Univ. Hamburg cycad seed guide; coning age from growers

shrub.source: Ryukyu cliffs and S Japan. A cycad, not a palm. Kew POWO.

bark.notes: trunk clad in persistent diamond-shaped leaf bases and brown woolly scales; shaggy pineapple-skin look

leaf.notes: stiff glossy dark green pinnate fronds in a circular rosette; narrow leaflets with rolled-under margins and sharp tips; new flush pale and woolly

flower.form: male: tall golden cone 30-60 cm; female: round woolly golden-brown dome of leaf-like scales

fruit.form: bright orange-red plum-like seeds 3-5 cm among the woolly female cone scales

appearance.seasonal: evergreen; none; annual flush of new leaves in one ring
appearance.silhouette: a stocky shaggy trunk 1-3 m topped with a symmetric dark green stiff feather rosette; branches/clumps with age
appearance.refs: Wikipedia Cycas revoluta; Kew POWO; Cycad Society

fruiting.source: Monaco Nature Encyclopedia (females: a golden, felted dome of leaf-like megasporophylls 14-22 cm; pollination mainly by insects May-July; seeds ovoid 3-5 x 2.5-3.5 cm, red-orange, mature Sep-Oct); Kono & Tobe 2007 (insect and wind pollination). Hang, set and crop estimated; seeds toxic (cycasin).

shrub.name: Australian cycad

growth.juvenile_note: Germination is hypogeal: the big seed sits on the soil while a taproot goes down. The first fronds are short with only a few pairs of narrow leaflets. For about a decade it is a stemless tuft of a few fronds per yearly flush over a swelling underground stem; then a stubby, fire-blackened trunk rises. Resprouts a whole new crown after dry-season fires.
growth.source: LLIFLE Cycas media (trunk usually 2.7-3.5 m, seldom 6 m; slow; seeds need months of after-ripening; refoliates after fire); Ornduff 1991 Bot. Gaz. 152 (C. media size classes, fire every 2-3 yr, beetles and Trigona bees at cones); Univ. Hamburg cycad seed guide. Growth rates estimated.

shrub.name: Modjadji cycad

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal germination; first leaves carry only 2-4 pairs of broad, spiny-edged leaflets. Stemless rosette over an underground stem for several years, but among the fastest cycads: leaves 1 m long in 4-5 years, then a thick trunk rises under an arching crown of long, glossy dark-green fronds with toothed leaflets.
growth.source: SANBI PlantZAfrica (1 m leaves in 4-5 yr; stem 12-13 m; cones in late summer; full sun or light shade; lives hundreds of years); treesa.org (stem 5-8 m, up to 13 m; relatively quick for a cycad); Univ. Hamburg cycad seed guide (sprouts ~1 month after cone disperses). Height curve and coning age estimated.

shrub.source: Modjadji, Limpopo; a forest of them. Tallest cycad. Kew POWO.

shrub.name: Coontie

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal: the orange seed stays on the ground while a single leaf appears bearing just one or two pairs of leaflets; later leaves carry more pairs. For years the plant is a small stemless tuft of stiff, dark green, feather-like leaves over a carrot-like underground stem; the stem usually stays buried, only its leafy crown showing.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Zamia integrifolia): stem 3-25 cm, often subterranean, leaves 20-100 cm with 5-30 pairs of leaflets; NC State Extension: slow-growing, sun to part shade, fleshy seed coat must be removed to germinate, 1-2 seeds can be fatal. Germination, growth, first coning and lifespan estimated from cycad cultivation.

shrub.name: Burrawang

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal: the big red-fleshed seed lies in the litter while a thick taproot and contractile roots pull the growing point down. The first leaf is a short frond with a few pairs of long narrow leaflets; for years it stays a small stemless tuft adding a few fronds a year over a swelling underground stem. The fountain of 50-100 arching 1-2 m fronds comes later; most plants never raise a visible trunk.
growth.source: Wikipedia (10-20 yr to maturity, lives to ~120 yr, huge underground tuber); ANBG Growing Native Plants (germination takes 6-24 months; trunk 0.3-2 m; 50-100 fronds to 2 m); ANPSA (very slow; cones after at least 10 yr); trunk emergence estimated
